summary.headline: V2 Retail Q4 FY26 revenue rose 60% YoY to Rs 797 crore and PAT hit a record Rs 17.5 crore; FY27 store target is 170-200.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 60% YoY to Rs 797 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 109 crore (13.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 17.5 crore versus Rs 6.4 crore a year earlier. FY26 revenue reached Rs 3,067 crore (+63%), with PAT of Rs 162 crore (+125%) and ROE of 26%. Management said the company added 136 stores in FY26 to reach 325 stores (about 3.5 million sq ft), and it guided to 170-200 stores in FY27 and at least 50% revenue growth over the next two years. Management also flagged a softer May due to geopolitical tension, with June expected to define the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: +89% YoY vs Rs 57.5 crore; margin up from 11.6%
+77% YoY vs Rs 258 crore; margin up from 13.7%
vs 23.2% in FY25 and about 10.7% in FY24

segments.name: Old stores (pre-FY24 vintage)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales per sq ft of Rs 1,124 for old stores; company-wide PSF reached about Rs 1,125 per management, with old-store EBITDA of about 11-12%.

segments.name: New stores (opened after FY24)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales per sq ft of Rs 750, about 70% of old-store level; store-level EBITDA about 5-6%, breakeven at about Rs 500 per sq ft, and 3-4 years to mature.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Men about 41-42%, women about 27%, kids about 25%. Kurtis, men's woven pajamas and men's casual shirts were the fastest-growing categories.

guidance_outlook: FY27 store additions targeted at 170-200, conditional on performance; management indicated about 250 stores in the following year, reaching about 500 by end FY27 per the Q&A.
Gross margin to be maintained at 28-30%; raw-material price rises to be passed on, with prices up about 3-4%.
At least 50% revenue growth guided over the next two years; SSSG guided at 8-10%.
FY27 EBITDA margins expected to be similar to FY26 and company PSF similar, as new-area additions of 50-60% offset SSSG and cost gains.
Inventory to be held at 90-100 days and creditors at 45 days; safety stock to be reduced once geopolitical situation normalises.
Marketing spend about 0.3% of revenue in FY26; FY27 expected to be below 0.5%.
Long-term aim of about 2,500 stores in India and Rs 1,200 per sq ft company-level PSF; 2,000-store milestone to be followed by a year of only about 500 new stores.
capex_capacity: Store count reached 325 with about 3.5 million sq ft; 33 stores opened and 2 closed in Q4, 136 net added in FY26; company crossed 350 stores per the opening remarks.
Capex per store about Rs 2.6 crore now, rising to Rs 2.7-2.8 crore including inventory; capex component about Rs 1.2-1.3 crore.
Per-sq-ft operating cost reduced from about Rs 200 to about Rs 190, targeted at about Rs 175.
Three zonal warehouses (central plus new Kolkata zonal, southern zonal being finalised) and about 18 hubs.
Store expansion to be funded from internal accruals and balance-sheet cash for FY27; debt preferred for any further funding.
demand_pricing: Early-season buying for festivals and wedding season, plus pre-GRC of Rs 100-150 crore, lifted March inventory; total additional inventory about Rs 300 crore including new-store stock.
Management said April was very good, May slow due to the war, and June expected to be one of the biggest months.
Average selling price about Rs 300; 3-4% price increase implies about Rs 10-12 added MRP.
Full-price share 90% in FY26; volume growth 47% vs revenue growth 63% attributed to product mix, with inflationary price increase of about 4-5%.
Management argued competitors' partial pass-through strategy would not be followed by V2.

qa_highlights.question: Store additions planned this year and funding source?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 stores in FY27, dependent on performance; funded by internal accruals and balance-sheet cash for at least this year, with debt as the first preference later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SSSG look weak in Q4 versus peers, and why did PSF fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 base is about Rs 1,000-1,040 per sq ft versus peers; management says FY SSSG still leads. Company PSF fell because new stores at about 70% of old-store PSF dilute the average; old-store PSF rose 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation jump in Q4 - one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a one-time accounting change: small items such as nuts, hard tags and hangers are now expensed rather than capitalised, impact about Rs 6-7 crore in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability and pass-through of yarn/cotton costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 28-30%, aided by better inventory freshness, inter-store transfers and less winter discounting; raw-material increases passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin flat with 50%+ area growth?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run at 5-6% EBITDA versus 11-12% for old stores, so blended margin stays flat until expansion slows; operating leverage expected to show from FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: Lease liabilities growing slower than area; why?
qa_highlights.answer: The company changed its lease accounting policy to look at 2-3 years of new-store performance; leases are about 1-year lock-ins and vendor lock-ins about 11 years, aligning with peers and narrowing the pre-IndAS to IndAS gap.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow positive while opening 175-200 stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected to stay positive; creditor days fell about 10 days due to vendor prepayments, which can be stopped if cash is needed for stores.

risks_watch: May slowdown linked to geopolitical tension; June trading to define Q1 FY27 performance.
Working capital: creditor days down about 10 days from prepayments; inventory at about 76% under 6 months old, with safety stock to be unwound later.
New stores at about 70% PSF and 5-6% EBITDA dilute company margins while new-area additions stay at 50-60%.
Store expansion to 170-200 in FY27 and 250 the following year depends on sustaining performance; expansion into newer states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, South) still at early stage.
Commodity and yarn price pass-through of 3-4% needs to hold volume; competitors reportedly taking partial margin hit.
Q4 depreciation step-up from expensing small items (about Rs 6-7 crore one-time).
summary.management_tone: Confident and long-term oriented on growth and store expansion, with repeated conditionality on performance. More cautious on the near term, acknowledging a slower May due to the war and declining company PSF from new-store dilution.
key_quotes: So, what we are building today is not for the near term. We are building for our 20 -year vision which is to be one of the top value fashion retailers in the country
So, we are guiding for the similar margins and the similar PSF.
So, about 76% of our inventory is less than 6 months old and out of that also about 50% of the inventory is less than 3 months old.

Kolkata zonal warehouse (new); southern zonal warehouse being finalised

growth.why: Management guides at least 50% revenue growth over FY27-FY28 and 170-200 store additions in FY27 (about 52% of the 325-store base, funded from internal accruals), with SSSG of 8-10%, though the store target is conditional on performance and May was softer due to geopolitical tension.
